Here is the Python code to classify the lines of the laboratory report:

```python
known_tests = {
    "718-7": "Haemoglobin",
    "789-8": "Red blood cells",
    "4544-3": "Haematocrit",
    "787-2": "MCV",
    "6690-2": "White blood cells",
    "777-3": "Platelets",
    "2498-4": "Iron",
    "2276-4": "Ferritin",
    "2345-7": "Glucose",
    "4548-4": "HbA1c",
    "2093-3": "Total cholesterol",
    "2085-9": "HDL cholesterol",
    "13457-7": "LDL cholesterol",
    "2571-8": "Triglycerides",
    "2160-0": "Creatinine",
    "3084-1": "Uric acid",
    "2951-2": "Sodium",
    "2823-3": "Potassium",
    "17861-6": "Calcium",
    "1742-6": "ALT",
    "1920-8": "AST",
    "2324-2": "GGT",
    "6768-6": "Alkaline phosphatase",
    "1975-2": "Total bilirubin",
    "1751-7": "Albumin",
    "3016-3": "TSH",
    "3024-7": "Free T4",
    "1988-5": "CRP",
    "62292-8": "Vitamin D (25-OH)",
    "2132-9": "Vitamin B12"
}

def classify_line(line):
    parts = line.split(":")
    number = parts[0].strip()
    test_name = parts[1].strip()
    if test_name in known_tests:
        return f"{number}|{known_tests[test_name]}"
    else:
        return f"{number}|NONE"

lines = [
    "1: Patient: Emma Smith    Date of birth: 01/06/2003",
    "2: Haemoglobin: 15.7 g/dl [12.0 - 16.0]",
    "3: Red blood cells: 4.8 10^6/µL [4.0 – 5.5]",
    "4: Haematocrit (HCT): 41.1 % [36.0 - 48.0]",
    "5: MCV: 87.9 fl [80.0 – 100.0]",
    "6: White. blood cells: 9.7 10^3/µL [4.0 - 10.0]",
    "7: Platelets (PLT): 221.4 10^3/uL [150.0 – 450.0]",
    "8: Iron: 235.0 ug/dL (H) [50.0-170.0]",
    "9: Ferritin: 98.7 ng/ml [15.0 - 150.0]",
    "10: Glucose: 50.3 mg/dL (L) [70.0 - 100.0]",
    "11: HbA1c: 3.5 % [<5.7]",
    "12: Total cholesterol: 282.7 mg/dl (H) [<200.0]",
    "13: HDL cholesterol: 27.6 mg/dL (L) [> 40.0]",
    "14: LDL. cholesterol: 87.3 mg/dL [up to 130.0]",
    "15: Triglycerides: 199.6 mg/dL (H) [< 150.0]",
    "16: Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL [0.5-1.1]",
    "17: Uric acid: 4.5 mg/dl [3.0 - 7.0]",
    "18: Na: 212.2 mmol/L (H) [136.0 – 145.0]",
    "19: Potassium: 4.1 mmol/L [3.5-5.1]",
    "20: Calcium: 10.4 mg/dL [8.5 – 10.5]",
    "21: ALT: 42.8 U/L (H) [up to 40.0]",
    "22: AST (GOT): 23.3 U/L [up to 40.0]",
    "23: GGT: 71.7 U/L [< 50.0]",
    "24: Alkaline phosphatase: 143.3 u/l (H) [40.0 – 130.0]",
    "25: Total bilirubin: 0.2 mg/dl (L) [0.3 – 1.2]",
    "26: Albumin: 5.6 g/dL (H) [3.5-5.0]",
    "27: TSH: 4.4 miu/l (H) [0.4 - 4.0]",
    "28: Free T4: 1.8 ng/dL (H) [0.9 – 1.7]",
    "29: CRP: 7.1 mg/l (H) [<5.0]",
    "30: Vitami. D (25-OH): 105.7 ng/mL (H) [30.0-100.0]",
    "31: Vitamin B12: 764.8 pg/mL [200.0-900.0]",
    "32: Pag. 1/1"
]

for line in lines:
    print(classify_line(line))
```

This code defines a dictionary `known_tests` that maps LOINC codes to their corresponding English names. The `classify_line` function takes a line from the report as input, splits it into parts, and checks if the test name is in the `known_tests` dictionary. If it is, the function returns a line with the number and the corresponding LOINC code. If not, the function returns a line with the number and "NONE". The code then iterates over the lines of the report, calls the `classify_line` function for each line, and prints the result.
